check: whether the name-based completeness check has blind spots that would make it report a false result on the pending run
why: The check compares expected names against reported names. Duplicate method names would collapse two cases into one, and a suite-level name carrying a dot would inflate the reported side. Both would produce a wrong verdict on the run it exists to judge.
duplicateNames: None. Extracting all 129 full names gives 129 distinct values with no group larger than one.
nameFormatMatches: The results file uses lowercase dotted names such as coldcaptureallocationtests.cancelledcoldviewdoesnotcancelitspeerorreleasetheforecastpin, which is the same class.method form the script builds from the source.
noSuiteNameContamination: The results file's testsuite element carries no name attribute, and a run of the script against the 2026-10-03 file reports 108 while that file holds exactly 108 testcase elements. So the reported side counts only cases.
whatTheCheckWillCatch: A class registered but not scheduled, a case renamed without the old one removed, and a case lost to a crash partway through the run. It compares names rather than only totals, which is what makes those visible.
whatItCannotCatch: A case that runs but asserts nothing, or one that passes without exercising its subject. Those were addressed separately - the filtered-stream assertions were given non-empty guards and the suite was checked for trivially-true assertions, empty lambdas, assertion-free methods and skip or retry mechanisms.
